after.prompt: You spotted Gold1 and Navy2 before moving. When should you look for them again?

options.text: Only once the puck is on your stick
Keep checking as you approach and before choosing your first touch
After you send the pass to Navy2

after.explanation: Gold1 and Navy2 can move while you approach. Keep checking pressure and support along with the puck, so your first touch fits the newest picture. Looking once does not finish the job.

before.prompt: If Gold1 closes YOU before the pass, what can Navy2 do?

options.text: Find Navy3 or another clear lane
Treat the planned pass as safe

after.prompt: Navy2 sees Gold1 closing from the inside. What could Navy2 call to help YOU before the pickup?
after.explanation: A short call such as “Pressure inside; I am along the boards” gives the pressure side and an outlet. YOU still checks the play: the call helps the scan and does not replace it.

after.prompt: If Gold1 wins the puck before YOU, what could Navy2 do?

options.text: Check Gold1’s route and look for a useful passing lane to close
Look toward the Navy net and recover to help defend
Keep waiting in the old spot for a pass from YOU

after.explanation: Gold1 now has possession, so Navy2’s job changes from offering an outlet to helping defend. Recovering or closing an available lane can help; if Navy2 can reach the puck under control, challenging it may also fit.

before.prompt: Why should YOU keep moving before the pass arrives?
before.explanation: Gold1 is close and can take away the first lane. Moving to a clear angle gives Navy2 a current target instead of a fixed one.

after.prompt: The puck is near where the side boards curve around the end of the rink. What do we call this area?
after.explanation: This is the corner. The slot is the middle space in front of the net; the point is near the attacking blue line. Naming the corner helps a teammate understand where the pickup is happening.
